newsitem.title: USA: U.S. crudes fade on inventory data, grades firming.
newsitem.headline: U.S. crudes fade on inventory data, grades firming.

text.p: U.S. cash crudes slipped Wednesday morning as a result of bearish inventory data contained in the weekly American Petroleum Institute and Department of Energy reports released from late Tuesday.
Outright prices for both July and August barrels edged lower on sentiment refinery output is outstripping demand.

The last day for July cash business featured a widening July/August roll and slightly firmer differentials for August grades. July grade prices were difficult to gauge, given the fact most refiners cleaned-up their needs previously.

Traders said the July/August roll sold at -35 and -36 cents, 6-8 cents weaker than Tuesday. July West Texas Intermediate/Cushing was pegged around $18.65-75 a barrel, around 10-15 cents weaker than yesterday, while outright August cash was down 10 cents at $18.95-$19.00 a barrel.
For the grades, Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James was charted at a 5-8 cents premium to the August benchmark, improving some 15 cents from July numbers on Tuesday.
August West Texas Sour/Midland talked at much weaker levels than July barrels did this week, around a $1.35 discount to the marker.
Eugene Island was pegged at $1.40-50 under WTI/Cushing, and Midland/WTI at 30-40 cents below level.
August WTI/Cushing Postings Plus barrels moved at $1.84, 20 cents stronger than July levels, working off a August/September roll at -17 cents.
